title: Vilikari — Laurels & Longhouses
label: chap:vilikari

overview.tagline: Two laws, one people. The oak remembers; the marble writes. The stone is cracking — and the dead are the only witnesses left.
overview.genre: Legal dualism, frontier identity crisis, forgotten treaties, hybrid survival.
overview.mood: Laurels, Longhouses, and the Weight of Witnesses
overview.starting_location: A longhouse quarter tucked into an old forum. Laurel garlands hang from broken columns. Smoke from a dozen hearths curls under cracked marble arches. A Hearth-Mother offers a cup of small beer and a piece of oatcake. 'The Foedus Stone cracks,' she says. 'The steppe listens. Which law will you speak when the Ykrul envoy arrives — oak or marble? The stone has a new crack. No one knows which promise it represents. Speak carefully. The stone is listening too. So is the Hollow. It always listens when a witness forgets.'

lore.history: The Vilikari are a people who refuse to choose. They do not pick between empire and steppe; they marry them, awkwardly, imperfectly, and with frequent arguments. Their halls are longhouses raised over ruined forums; their laws carved on both oak and marble; their loyalties braided like the war-maidens' hair. They are the bulk of the non-elite population in Ecktoria — the legionaries' descendants who never went home. A Vilikari blacksmith in Ecktoria might swear by the marble bench; his cousin two valleys over in Acasia still ties knots for the oak. This is not contradiction. It is survival. But survival requires witnesses, and the witnesses are dying. The Foedus Stone, ancient guarantor of their autonomy, is cracking. Every season, another shard falls. The Ecktorian clerks have stopped renewing the oath; the Ykrul no longer send hostages. The Vilikari are becoming invisible to both sides. Their law still holds, but the witnesses are fading. The Elder of Elders speaks once a year, but fewer and fewer listen. The newest crack appeared last winter. It has no date. No one knows which promise it represents. Some Vilikari elders still whisper the name Crom (or Krom) when they speak of the power that breaks chains. On the coast, fishing villages double as smugglers' coves, running fugitives, forbidden goods, and whispered messages. They are the last people in the Amaranthine who still remember the old treaty's third clause. They are not sure why it matters. They keep it anyway.
lore.first_notice: Woodsmoke and old parchment. The way everyone speaks two languages at once — switching mid-sentence. Longhouse roofs that use broken imperial tiles as shingles. The silence where there used to be oaths. The way old men press their ears to stone, listening for a promise that has not yet been spoken.
lore.rule_that_kills: Never invoke only one law. The mallus (oak-ring) and the basilica (marble bench) must both be honored. Choose one, and the other will find you. But now, neither may answer. The stone has forgotten which law applies — so it applies neither. The Hollow has begun to remember the forgotten clauses instead.

entanglements.south: Ecktoria — Imperial clerks still claim suzerainty over the Foedus Stone; the two-laws dialectic is a full-time occupation. The Archivolt has a sealed file on every Vilikari family. The clerks are starting to misplace those files. The stone is not.
entanglements.north: Ykrul — Hostage strings and grazing rights are the currency of the border; the Khagan's envoys speak in proverbs. The Foedus Stone cracks a little more each season. The envoys have stopped sending hostages. They are waiting for the stone to forget.
entanglements.southeast: Acasia — Broken Marches mercenaries often find work in the longhouses; the Curse of Acasia is a rumor here, but the smoke from the south smells of burning promises. The Curse does not cross the border. The stone is not so sure.
entanglements.coast: The Amaranthine Coast — Vilikari smugglers and fishermen are indistinguishable, running today's catch and contraband past the lantern-law. They are the only ones who still profit from the cracks. They do not ask where the cargo comes from. They do not ask where it goes.

regional_diagnostic.current_hook: The stone is cracking. Find a witness older than the stone itself to renew the treaty.
regional_diagnostic.core_conflict: The Vilikari are the bridge between empire and wilderness — the marriage of oak-law and marble-law — but the witnesses who validate that bridge are dying, and neither Ecktoria nor Ykrul sends hostages anymore. The Ninth is the forgotten witness; the Hollow is the silence of the stone.
regional_diagnostic.unique_feature: **The Weight of the Crack:** the Foedus Stone is a living, cracking legal artifact; every jurisdictional conflict, every broken oath, and every forgotten promise widens a crack that, when complete, erases the Vilikari as a recognized people. The cracks are full of truths the stone could not hold.
regional_diagnostic.ninth_taboo: In Vilikari courts, the ninth witness called to a mallus (oak-ring) is always a ghost. The wise stop at eight and settle out of court. Those who call a ninth witness find that the ghost speaks the truth — but the truth is always the worst possible version, and the living witnesses remember it as their own. The stone's cracks are full of these truths. The Hollow drinks them.
regional_diagnostic.price: Players sacrifice **memory, legal standing, or reputation** to gain power. Every reward requires a gamble: a forgotten clause, a cracked seal, a promise to a dying witness, or a name given to the Hollow.

faction_triad.goal: Preserve imperial forms, patents, and the marble bench's authority
faction_triad.method: Charters, patents, Utaran precedent, the Queen's audience
faction_triad.why_players_care: Marble-High status grants +1 Effect citing charters and patents

faction_triad.goal: Preserve tribal custom, blood-price, and the oak-ring's authority
faction_triad.method: Wergild tables, oath-braids, the Elder of Elders' nod
faction_triad.why_players_care: Oak-High status grants +1 Position invoking mallus or blood-price

faction_triad.goal: Keep the old treaty's forgotten third clause alive through trade, not law
faction_triad.method: Lantern-law evasion, contraband routes, cargo loyalty
faction_triad.why_players_care: The only faction that still profits while the stone cracks

quotes.speaker: Federate King Aldric (Elite)
quotes.text: We are the bridge between empire and wilderness, the marriage of law and custom. Our strength lies not in choosing one path but in walking both with equal surety. But the bridge is rotting, and no one sends hostages anymore. The stone cracks, and the cracks have no witnesses. I hear the Hollow in the cracks. It is learning our laws faster than we remember them.

quotes.speaker: Hearth-Mother Vesna (Commoner)
quotes.text: The old ways and new laws both have their place at our table. Serve the right mead to the right guest, honor the proper customs, and you'll find we're better hosts than most kings. The trouble is, the guests are forgetting why they came. The stone is forgetting their names. I set a plate for the Hollow every night. It hasn't come yet — but it is learning how to knock.

witness_fading_timer.name: Witness Fading
advance_on: The party defies a Vilikari judgment or brings a dispute to an outside court (+1)
A foreign envoy publicly ignores a Vilikari ruling (+1)
The GM spends 2 SB to represent a forgotten oath (+1)

thresholds.4: The stone's cracks are visible to all. Vilikari NPCs suffer -1 die on social rolls (they are losing faith in their own law).
thresholds.8: The Foedus Stone cracks completely. The Vilikari are no longer recognized as neutral. Ykrul and Ecktorians begin fighting over their land. Reset only by renewing the treaty: finding a witness older than the stone itself and having them speak the oath aloud.

stirrs_table.complication: A forgotten clause surfaces — a promise owed to a dead man. Fulfill it or the crack widens (tick Witness Fading +1).
A ghost witness appears in a mallus. It demands the ninth witness be called. The Hollow is listening.
A Foedus Seal you carry cracks. It can still be used once more — but it will crumble afterward.
The Elder of Elders forgets a name. He asks you to remind him. If you cannot, the stone takes the memory instead.
A Ykrul envoy offers a hostage — but the hostage is a ghost. The Hollow has already claimed them.
The stone weeps water that tastes of salt and iron. The water is the memory of a treaty broken by both sides.
A Vilikari war-maiden cuts her braid. The dead she carried are now unclaimed. The Hollow will find them within a week.
The marble bench and the oak-ring are the same temperature. The stone has stopped distinguishing between them.

two_law_tension.name: Two-Law Tension
two_law_tension.advance_on: Whenever a jurisdictional conflict arises (mallus vs. basilica), players may step Position up by citing the Foedus Stone or an older precedent — but every use adds a tick.

thresholds.4: One side demands exclusive authority. If Witness Fading is at 4+, this timer ticks twice as fast.

npcs.name: Hearth-Mother Vesna
npcs.motivation: Preserve hospitality and memory as the stone forgets
npcs.quirk: She has never lost a quarrel; her voice is soft, her memory longer than the Foedus Stone. She remembers obligations that are not yet owed — and the stone is forgetting, shrinking.

npcs.name: Shield-Brother Rurik
npcs.motivation: Keep every oath he has ever sworn
npcs.quirk: His braids are his record; each knot is an oath kept — or broken. He has started tying knots in his sleep, hoping the stone will remember. The Hollow knows every knot he has tied.

npcs.name: March Notary Theodora
npcs.quirk: Her left hand writes Utaran, her right writes runes. She signs with her foot. A 'third hand' writes in ink that no one can read — not even her. The ink is from the stone's cracks.

npcs.name: Ykrul Envoy
npcs.motivation: Speak obligations in proverbs and keep the border quiet
npcs.quirk: He never carries a weapon. His tongue is sharp enough. His hostage string has nine knots. He is running out of space — and the stone is running out of memory. The Hollow has already forgotten his name.

npcs.name: Old Legionary
npcs.motivation: Keep the old imperial discipline alive in muscle memory
npcs.quirk: He still marks time in paces. The recruits call him 'Grandfather Eagle.' The eagle on his shield is chipped. He presses his ear to the stone at night. He has heard it whisper his own death.

npcs.name: Marcher-Lord
npcs.motivation: Hold the border without losing either law
npcs.quirk: His crown was a plowshare. His hands are still calloused. He does not sit on his throne. He spends his days pressing his ear to the stone. It is warm.

npcs.name: War-Maiden
npcs.motivation: Remember the dead and the owed
npcs.quirk: Her braid is longer than her sword. Both have drawn blood. She never cuts the braid. The dead would forget her. The stone is forgetting everyone else. She has started braiding in her own hair.

npcs.name: Federate King Aldric
npcs.motivation: Hold three thrones — oak, marble, and saddle — without losing any
npcs.quirk: He has three thrones — oak, marble, and saddle. He uses whichever is not being argued over. Lately, all three are dusty. He has stopped arguing. He just listens to the stone. It is whispering the names of the dead.

npcs.name: Elder of Elders
npcs.motivation: Preserve the original treaty before he forgets it entirely
npcs.quirk: He speaks once a year. The rest of the time he listens — and remembers. But his memory is cracking like the stone. He has started writing things on his own skin. The Hollow reads his skin at night.

npcs.name: Smuggler Captain Drago
npcs.motivation: Profit from the cracks no one else is watching
npcs.quirk: He runs contraband and refugees past the Kahfagian patrols, knows every reef and lantern shift, and claims the stone's cracks are good for business — no one checks the old treaties anymore. The Hollow pays in silver.

places.title: Longhouse Quarter
places.subtitle: [COMMUNITY]
places.description: The forum's marble floor is worn smooth by dancing feet, not sandals.
places.flavor: The ghosts of tax collectors weep in the corners. The ghosts of Ykrul hostages sing in the rafters. The stone is forgetting which is which.
places.mechanical_hook: Resting here clears 1 Fatigue and grants +1 die to the next social roll invoking hospitality, if the Hearth-Mother is honored properly.

places.title: Milefort XVII
places.subtitle: [MILITARY]
places.description: Earth bank, stone gate; faded eagle over fresh knotwork.
places.flavor: The eagle's stone wings were reglued after a lightning strike. It still leans left — toward the steppe. The stone's crack points the same way.
places.mechanical_hook: Garrison here grants a Cap 2 defensive advantage in any skirmish, but housing here for more than a night starts a minor Border Tension tick.

places.title: Stone Ford
places.subtitle: [TRADE]
places.description: Plank-palings and a customs table at knee-height; border as bureaucracy.
places.flavor: The ford changes hands every season. The customs table never moves. The wood is stained with ink and blood. The stone's crack drinks both.
places.mechanical_hook: A held Diamond may be cashed as currency here one-for-one, creating a Stone Weight the GM may call in later.

places.title: Villa Granary
places.subtitle: [MILITARY]
places.description: Barracks with a tile roof; spear racks where olives once slept.
places.flavor: The olive press still works. The pressers are now armorers. The oil is for lamps, not cooking. The oil is also for anointing the stone.
places.mechanical_hook: Requisitioning supplies here requires a Sway or Command roll (DV 4); success grants 1 Supply, failure ticks Annona Late.

places.title: Twin Court
places.subtitle: [LAW]
places.description: Mallus ring beneath an oak, basilica bench across the lane.
places.flavor: The oak and the bench are the same distance from the well. The well is neutral ground. The well has a chain. The chain is warm.
places.mechanical_hook: A judgment rendered here under both laws simultaneously reduces the Two-Law Tension timer by 1 instead of ticking it. The well's chain will hold the oath.

places.title: Blackwood Road
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
places.description: Milestones re-carved in runes and Utaran both.
places.flavor: The runes say 'safe passage.' The Utaran says 'toll payable twice.' The third line is scratched out. The scratching is the Hollow's signature.
places.mechanical_hook: Travel along this road is faster (−1 segment on travel timers) but tolls are demanded twice — once per law.

places.title: Staple Market
places.subtitle: [TRADE] [SOCIAL]
places.description: Frontier where Ykrul horses meet Vilikari iron.
places.flavor: The horse-traders and smiths speak a pidgin of gestures and grudges. The scales are honest — mostly. The stone's crack is the third scale.
places.mechanical_hook: Converting a held Diamond into a Market Edge (+1 die to buy/sell rolls for the scene) ticks Market Knives [4].

places.title: Burial Field
places.subtitle: [DEATH]
places.description: Ship-ridge mounds beside tiled mausolea, both garlanded.
places.flavor: The mausolea have fresh offerings. The ancestors are not picky. The ship-mounds whisper at dawn. The whispers are in a language the stone has forgotten.
places.mechanical_hook: Disturbing the field risks the Grave Offense complication; honoring it grants a Boon on the next Lore roll about Vilikari history.

places.title: Repaired Bridge
places.subtitle: [TRAVEL] [LAW]
places.description: An arch of stone, a Vilikari trestle stitched on; past and present joined.
places.flavor: The trestle creaks in Vilikari, the stone groans in Utaran. They argue at midnight. The toll-keeper listens. The Hollow listens too.
places.mechanical_hook: Diamonds tied to rights or escorts may be cashed as currency here one-for-one, same as Stone Ford.

places.title: Hill Amphitheater
places.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
places.description: A lord's hall raised in an old arena's curve; power in architecture.
places.flavor: The lord's throne is a gladiator's chair. He does not know who last sat in it. The sand beneath is still dark. The stone's crack runs through the center.
places.mechanical_hook: Holding court here grants +1 Position to whoever sits the throne, but any challenge to their authority happens publicly, before witnesses.

places.title: New Raivon
places.subtitle: [URBAN]
places.description: March capital; grid-streets colliding with wandering lanes.
places.flavor: The grid was laid by a surveyor who never came back. The lanes are older. They move at night. The stone's cracks are the surveyor's map.
places.mechanical_hook: Navigating the city at night requires a Wits+Lore roll (DV 4) or the party arrives somewhere other than intended, though rarely somewhere unhelpful.

places.title: Dux's Palace
places.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
places.description: Purple awnings, wolf-hides, law tablets on the wall.
places.flavor: The tablets list every treaty broken. The wolf-hides are from the treaty-breakers. They still growl. The stone's cracks match their teeth marks.
places.mechanical_hook: Reading the tablets grants a genuine piece of GM-provided history about a broken treaty relevant to the current plot.

places.title: Foedus Stone
places.subtitle: [LAW] [LEGEND]
places.description: At a crossroads; every treaty carved, every hand weighed.
places.flavor: The stone has grown. Each new treaty adds a finger of granite. The oldest fingers are worn smooth. The newest crack has no date. The stone is warm. The Hollow is close.
places.mechanical_hook: An oath sworn here is doubly binding; if the Witness Fading Timer is at 4+, the stone glows, and the next legal argument made here is automatically binding for both sides (Crack Light).

people_and_factions.title: Hearth-Mother Vesna
people_and_factions.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
people_and_factions.flavor: She has never lost a quarrel; her voice is soft, her memory longer than the Foedus Stone. She remembers obligations that are not yet owed — and the stone is forgetting, shrinking.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: She'll grant guest-right (safe hospitality) to anyone who serves the correct mead to the correct guest, once.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: Proper observance of custom, and news of the wider marches.

people_and_factions.title: Shield-Brother Rurik
people_and_factions.subtitle: [MILITARY] [OATH]
people_and_factions.flavor: His braids are his record; each knot is an oath kept — or broken. He has started tying knots in his sleep, hoping the stone will remember. The Hollow knows every knot he has tied.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll fight alongside the party in one engagement, if their cause is oath-bound and genuine.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A knot tied in his braid — a public record of the debt owed to him.

people_and_factions.title: March Notary Theodora
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LAW]
people_and_factions.flavor: Her left hand writes Utaran, her right writes runes. She signs with her foot. A 'third hand' writes in ink that no one can read — not even her. The ink is from the stone's cracks.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: She'll draft a document binding under both laws simultaneously, once, for a case she believes is just.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A fee paid in salt or coin, and total honesty about the case's true stakes.

people_and_factions.title: Horse-Reeve
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRADE]
people_and_factions.description: Rations pasture between plows and warbands.
people_and_factions.flavor: He measures grass in fistfuls. The Ykrul respect his arithmetic. The Ecktorians pretend not to notice. He is saving fistfuls to patch the stone.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll allocate grazing rights or fodder to the party's mounts, once, if they respect his measurements.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A fistful of grain, symbolically given toward patching the stone.

people_and_factions.title: Ykrul Envoy
people_and_factions.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
people_and_factions.description: Riding under safe-conduct; speaks obligations in proverbs.
people_and_factions.flavor: He never carries a weapon. His tongue is sharp enough. His hostage string has nine knots. He is running out of space — and the stone is running out of memory. The Hollow has already forgotten his name.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll broker a minor understanding between the party and the Ykrul, once, if approached with correct proverb-etiquette.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A proverb answered honestly, and patience with the ritual of negotiation.

people_and_factions.title: Old Legionary
people_and_factions.subtitle: [MILITARY]
people_and_factions.description: Drill-master for Vilikari levies; Utar in muscle memory.
people_and_factions.flavor: He still marks time in paces. The recruits call him 'Grandfather Eagle.' The eagle on his shield is chipped. He presses his ear to the stone at night. He has heard it whisper his own death.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll train the party in formation discipline, once, granting a Cap bonus in their next organized engagement.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: Genuine effort and respect for the old drills — he has no patience for shortcuts.

people_and_factions.title: Ecktorial Factor
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRADE]
people_and_factions.description: Vilikari blood, Ecktorial coin; flows where the market points.
people_and_factions.flavor: His coat has two collars — one for each loyalty. He wears whichever is warmer. His tally has three columns. The third column is labeled 'crack width.'
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll broker a trade deal across the Ecktorian border, once, for a cut of the profit.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A percentage of the deal, and discretion about which collar he wore that day.

people_and_factions.title: Kahfagian Pilot
people_and_factions.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
people_and_factions.description: Lantern-law chit and clan tattoo; sea-law on land.
people_and_factions.flavor: He navigates by stars and tariffs. Both change with the season. He has never been lost — only delayed. The stone's cracks are good for smuggling.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll pilot the party past the lantern-law patrols, once, no questions asked about cargo.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A cut of whatever's being moved, and discretion in return.

people_and_factions.title: Marcher-Lord
people_and_factions.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
people_and_factions.description: Iron-nail crown, Vilikari law in pocket; a frontier king.
people_and_factions.flavor: His crown was a plowshare. He reversed the curse. His hands are still calloused. He does not sit on his throne. He spends his days pressing his ear to the stone. It is warm.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: He'll grant a minor writ or land-right, once, to anyone who helps him understand what the stone is telling him.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: Genuine effort toward understanding the stone's cracks, not empty flattery.

people_and_factions.title: War-Maiden
people_and_factions.subtitle: [COMBAT] [OATH]
people_and_factions.description: Oath-braid names the dead and the owed; vengeance as memory.
people_and_factions.flavor: Her braid is longer than her sword. Both have drawn blood. She never cuts the braid. The dead would forget her. The stone is forgetting everyone else. She has started braiding in her own hair.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: She'll pursue a vengeance-oath alongside the party, once, if the wrong is genuine and the target named.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A place in her braid — the party's names become part of her record, for better or worse.

people_and_factions.title: Queen of Marches
people_and_factions.subtitle: [POLITICS]
people_and_factions.flavor: She married the Federate King for peace. She kept the kingdom for herself. Her seal is a broken arrow. She keeps a piece of the stone in her pocket — it gets smaller every year.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: A private audience with her can turn a whisper into policy — rare, and never without a price.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A secret, or a service that only a trusted outsider could perform.

people_and_factions.title: Federate King Aldric
people_and_factions.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
people_and_factions.description: Rex-Dux sworn to forms, sung by his own.
people_and_factions.flavor: He has three thrones — oak, marble, and saddle. He uses whichever is not being argued over. Lately, all three are dusty. He has stopped arguing. He just listens to the stone. It is whispering the names of the dead.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: His formal favor is rare and binding under all three of his thrones' authority at once.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: Public loyalty, demonstrated in a manner of his choosing.

people_and_factions.title: Elder of Elders
people_and_factions.subtitle: [LAW]
people_and_factions.description: Thing-council speaker; a nod can unmake a clan.
people_and_factions.flavor: He speaks once a year. The rest of the time he listens — and remembers. But his memory is cracking like the stone. He has started writing things on his own skin. The Hollow reads his skin at night.
people_and_factions.what_they_carry: His yearly words carry the weight of ancient precedent — genuine, cryptic, and binding on those who hear them.
people_and_factions.what_they_ask: A memory, freely given, to help him remember what the stone is forgetting.

complications.title: Annona Late
complications.subtitle: [SUPPLY] [SOCIAL]
complications.description: Grain stipend misses the comitatus; tempers quicken like flint.
complications.flavor: The granary is full. The keys are in the wrong vault. Someone is waiting for the price to rise. The soldiers are not. The stone does not care.
complications.mechanical_hook: Resolving the shortage requires a Sway or Investigation roll (DV 4); failure ticks a relevant Supply timer by 1.

complications.title: Law Tangle
complications.subtitle: [LAW]
complications.description: Mallus verdict vs. basilica writ — whose seal bites?
complications.flavor: The oak judge and the marble judge are cousins. They send each other holiday cards. The case has been open for three generations. The stone has forgotten who started it.
complications.mechanical_hook: Citing the Foedus Stone or older precedent steps Position up but adds a tick to the Two-Law Tension [4] timer.

complications.title: Raid Rumor
complications.subtitle: [COMBAT] [FEAR]
complications.description: A Ykrul boyar; levies panic the plowlands.
complications.flavor: The boyar is a ghost — or a tax collector. The farmers don't wait to find out. They burn the fields themselves. The stone's cracks are good cover for ghosts.
complications.mechanical_hook: Investigating before the farmers panic (Wits+Lore, DV 4) prevents the fields from burning; failure costs the region 1 Supply.

complications.title: Bridge Levy
complications.subtitle: [TRADE] [COMBAT]
complications.description: Doubled for road-works; caravans balk, fists rise.
complications.flavor: The road-works are a ditch. The ditch fills every spring. The bridge keeper has a new sword. He sharpens it on the stone.
complications.mechanical_hook: Paying the levy costs 1 Supply; refusing risks a Cap 2 confrontation with the bridge keeper's hired men.

complications.title: Succession Feud
complications.subtitle: [POLITICS] [DEATH]
complications.flavor: The wolf-brother has a better sword. The purple-charter has a better notary. The notary's ink is mixed with blood. The stone's crack drinks it.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party must choose a side or broker peace via a Wergild Table (Sway DV 5); refusal starts a Feud Spiral timer.

complications.title: Foedus Recall
complications.subtitle: [LAW] [SOCIAL]
complications.description: A prefecture resettlement is 'requested'; homes bristle.
complications.flavor: The prefecture's map is forty years old. It shows a village that drowned. The villagers are still there. The stone remembers their names — barely.
complications.mechanical_hook: Resolving the dispute peacefully requires producing a valid counter-charter (Wits+Lore, DV 5) or accepting the Witness Fading Timer ticking by 1.

complications.title: Coin Talk
complications.subtitle: [TRADE] [WEIGHT]
complications.description: Debasement; pay demanded in salt, hides, or hostages.
complications.flavor: The salt is from a disputed pan. The hides are from cattle that were never born. The hostages are children. The stone's cracks are full of their names.
complications.mechanical_hook: Negotiating fair payment requires a Sway roll (DV 5); failure risks a hostage being taken as collateral.

complications.title: Grave Offense
complications.subtitle: [DEATH] [OMEN]
complications.description: A burial field disturbed; omens ride with the news.
complications.flavor: The ancestors are angry. They have a list. Your name may be on it. The list is carved on a ship's prow. The stone's new crack is shaped like a finger pointing.
complications.mechanical_hook: Making amends (an offering, a proper reburial) clears the omen; ignoring it imposes a Condition (Ill-Omened) on the offending party.

complications.title: Port Clash
complications.subtitle: [LAW] [TRADE]
complications.flavor: The lanterns were moved last night. The old safe channel is now a reef. The harbor master is not answering questions. He is listening to the stone.
complications.mechanical_hook: Navigating the port without a Foedus Seal or lantern-law chit forces a Desperate Boating or Subterfuge roll (DV 5).

complications.title: Warband Flip
complications.subtitle: [MILITARY] [BETRAYAL]
complications.description: Colors change mid-pay; hostage protocol snaps shut.
complications.flavor: The hostages are eating well. Their captors are not. The captain's new banner is stitched with his old captain's hair. The stone's crack has grown wider.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party's allied warband may defect unless a Loyalty-testing scene (Sway DV 5) succeeds before the pay comes due.

complications.title: Restoration Preacher
complications.subtitle: [SOCIAL] [FEAR]
complications.description: Stirs crowds against the 'barbarian king in purple.'
complications.flavor: The preacher's license was signed by a dead abbot. The seal is still warm. The crowd does not know. The stone does not care.
complications.mechanical_hook: Exposing the preacher's forged license (Investigation DV 5) disperses the crowd; failure risks a riot (Cap 2).

complications.title: General Levy
complications.subtitle: [MILITARY] [SUPPLY]
complications.description: The march is closed; markets freeze into spears.
complications.flavor: The levy notice is posted in three languages. None of them are local. The tax collector has a bow. The stone has stopped listening.
complications.mechanical_hook: The party is conscripted into the levy unless they can produce a valid exemption (a writ, a Purple Warrant, or a lord's favor).

complications.title: Spring Melt
complications.subtitle: [WEATHER] [TRAVEL]
complications.description: Eats the Wolf Road; proofs, plans, and armies bog.
complications.flavor: The road is a memory. The ruts fill with water — and older things. The bridge keeper is fishing for boots. The stone's crack is now a chasm.
complications.mechanical_hook: Travel along affected roads is Desperate until the melt subsides; a Miss risks losing cargo or a mount to the mud.

rewards.title: Foedus Seal
rewards.subtitle: [LAW]
rewards.description: Settlement and stipends confirmed for a season.
rewards.flavor: The seal is a bronze wolf's head. It warms when the treaty holds — and cools when it doesn't. The wolf's eyes are garnets. One eye is cracked.
rewards.curse_cost: The seal's warmth is a visible, public indicator of the treaty's health — everyone can see when it's cooling.

rewards.title: Mallus Right
rewards.subtitle: [LAW]
rewards.description: Hold court under the oak and be obeyed.
rewards.flavor: The oak is older than the kingdom. Its roots have seen more verdicts than the throne. The acorns are bitter. The oak's leaves are falling early.
rewards.curse_cost: Rulings made under Mallus Right are not recognized by marble-law courts, and vice versa.

rewards.title: Stipend Arrears
rewards.subtitle: [SUPPLY]
rewards.description: Paid in salt and grain; portable, persuasive.
rewards.flavor: The salt is gray. The grain is from last harvest. Both are worth more than coin. The soldiers will accept. The stone will not.
rewards.curse_cost: The stipend is a one-time payment; asking for a second draws suspicion of overreach.

rewards.title: Utaran Patent
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
rewards.description: Citizenship-style privilege; doors open, bows deepen.
rewards.flavor: The patent is a worn scrap of vellum. It has been folded and refolded for a century. The seal is a sunburst. The sunburst is fading.
rewards.curse_cost: The patent's authority is fading along with the seal — its protections weaken as the Witness Fading Timer rises.

rewards.title: Stall-Right
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE]
rewards.description: Customs favor on a frontier market line.
rewards.flavor: The stall is a painted plank. Plant it, and the tax man will pretend not to see you. He will remember the favor. The stone will not.
rewards.curse_cost: The favor is personal, not transferable, and expires if the tax man is replaced.

rewards.title: Hostage Treaty
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL] [OATH]
rewards.description: Exchange fosters; grudges trade for leverage.
rewards.flavor: The hostages are children. Their parents are patient. The treaty has nine clauses. The ninth is unspoken. The stone has forgotten the first eight.
rewards.curse_cost: The unspoken ninth clause will eventually be invoked by the other side, on their terms, not yours.

rewards.title: Remount Allotment
rewards.subtitle: [TRAVEL]
rewards.description: Fresh horses from royal paddocks, no questions.
rewards.flavor: The horses are from the king's own herd. They know the roads better than you. They also know the king's secrets. They refuse to cross the stone's shadow.
rewards.curse_cost: The horses will not approach the Foedus Stone or any place its shadow reaches — a real, mechanical limitation on their use.

rewards.title: Wergild Table
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [WEIGHT]
rewards.description: Recognized by both codes; vengeance priced and paid.
rewards.flavor: The table is a slate slab. The prices are carved deep — and often recarved. The newest price is a year of rain. The rain is washing away the carvings.
rewards.curse_cost: Prices on the table shift over time as the carvings wash away — what was owed may change by the time it's collected.

rewards.title: Bridge Farm
rewards.subtitle: [TRADE]
rewards.description: Imperial for a season; funds and friends accrue.
rewards.flavor: The bridge toll is a copper a head. The bridge keeper is your new best friend. He also keeps a list of your enemies. He scratches the list on the stone.
rewards.curse_cost: The bridge keeper's friendship comes with his enmities attached — your enemies become his business too.

rewards.title: Purple Warrant
rewards.subtitle: [AUTHORITY]
rewards.description: Wear the stripe; officials defer on sight.
rewards.flavor: The stripe is a sash. It was a curtain in a past life. The present life is yours. Do not lose it. The stone's crack has swallowed one like it.
rewards.curse_cost: Losing the warrant is a serious loss of face and legal standing — it cannot easily be replaced.

rewards.title: Queen's Audience
rewards.subtitle: [SOCIAL]
rewards.flavor: The audience is held in a garden. The flowers are listening. The gardener is a spy. The gardener is also the queen. She keeps a piece of the stone under her tongue.
rewards.curse_cost: What is whispered becomes policy for everyone, not just the asker, and can be reversed by rivals with better arguments.

rewards.title: Dux Commission
rewards.subtitle: [MILITARY]
rewards.description: Command a mixed unit with pay authority.
rewards.flavor: The commission is a baton. It doubles as a mace in a pinch. It also doubles as a receipt. The receipt is overdue. The stone has a receipt for the stone.
rewards.curse_cost: The pay authority comes with an overdue debt attached — someone, somewhere, expects repayment for the commission.

rewards.title: Great Law Day
rewards.subtitle: [LAW] [LEGEND]
rewards.description: Proclaim a new concord; one temporary exception to old law.
rewards.flavor: The proclamation is made at noon. By sunset, everyone will have an opinion. By dawn, the Foedus Stone will have a new finger — or a new crack.
rewards.curse_cost: The outcome (a new finger of granite, or a new crack) is decided by the GM based on how the exception was used — not guaranteed to favor the party.

quick_use_notes.draw_rules: Draw until you have all four suits: Spade = place, Heart = actor, Club = pressure, Diamond = leverage. Highest rank sets the main Timer (2–5 → 4 segments, 6–10 → 6 segments, J/Q/K → 8 segments, A → 10 segments).
quick_use_notes.diamonds: Diamonds are codified outcomes (charters, rights, escorts) that change position rather than call for a roll.
quick_use_notes.ace_rule: If any Ace appears, echo law and bond motifs — oaths that bind, stones that witness, treaties that remember every hand — but also cracks and forgetting. The stone's newest crack widens; the Hollow listens.

what_players_actually_do: Resolve legal disputes between oak-law and marble-law factions, often involving charters, treaties, and wergild.
Navigate frontier diplomacy between Ecktoria, Ykrul, and the Federate King's court.
Smuggle or trade through contested passes, fords, and markets.
Investigate the Foedus Stone — its cracks, its history, and the forgotten clauses that could reshape the region.

core_timers.witness_fading: **[8]** Tracks the erosion of Vilikari legal authority. Ticks when: the party defies a Vilikari judgment or brings a dispute to an outside court (+1); the GM spends 2 SB to represent a forgotten oath (+1); a foreign envoy publicly ignores a Vilikari ruling (+1). At 4 segments: any Vilikari NPC the party interacts with suffers −1 die to social rolls. At 8 segments: the Foedus Stone cracks completely — the Vilikari are no longer recognized as neutral, and the Ykrul and Ecktorians begin fighting over their land. Reset only by renewing the treaty: finding a witness older than the stone itself and having them speak the oath aloud.
core_timers.two_law_tension: **[4]** Whenever a jurisdictional conflict arises (mallus vs. basilica), players may step Position up by citing the Foedus Stone or an older precedent — but every use adds a tick. When it fills, one side demands exclusive authority. If Witness Fading is at 4+, this timer ticks twice as fast.
core_timers.border_tension_front: Once per session, if a deal is struck with a foreign envoy or mixed-blood courtier, advance or start this front.
core_timers.market_knives: **[4]** At any Staple Market or Stone Ford, converting a held Diamond into a Market Edge (+1 die to buy/sell rolls) ticks this timer. When full, a rival factor challenges your right to trade — a duel, a bribe demand, or a confiscation.
core_timers.feast_bond_blood_owed: **[3] / [3]** Created by the Treaty-Feast Procedure. While Feast-Bond has segments, both parties are protected from betrayal in that matter. On breach, the breaker immediately takes 1–2 SB and the timer flips to Blood-Owed [3].

additional_features.two_law_dial: **Oak High:** +1 Position when invoking mallus, blood-price, or tribal custom; the first basilica petition starts one step worse. **Marble High:** +1 Effect when citing charters, patents, or Utaran precedent; the first mallus oath starts one step worse. Center the dial by offering a wergild recognized by both sides or hosting a joint moot. If Witness Fading is at 4+, centering requires a sacrifice (a memory, a name, or a drop of blood on the stone).
additional_features.frontier_diplomacy: If a Heart card involves a foreign envoy, a federate, or a mixed-blood courtier, treat the first Diamond played in the scene as doubled leverage. If Witness Fading is at 6+, the deal also ticks the timer by 1.
additional_features.march_markets: At any Staple Market, Stone Ford, or Repaired Bridge, Diamonds tied to rights or escorts may be cashed as currency in lieu of coin, one-for-one. Doing so creates a Stone Weight the GM may call in later through factions or raiders.
additional_features.vilikari_diaspora: Vilikari characters in Ecktoria gain +1 die on Subterfuge checks but −1 die on social rolls with Old Blood patricians. In Acasia, they gain +1 die on Survival checks but −1 die on social rolls with the Curse-touched. A Vilikari character may start with one 'family tally' — a minor asset tracking a single unpaid favor across generations. If Witness Fading ever fills, the tally turns to ash.
treaty_feast_procedure: Set the Table: name 2–3 terms (what both sides want) and 1 taboo (off-limits).
First Cup (Position): roll a social test; success grants +1 die to bargain, failure grants the host 1 SB.
Bread & Salt (Offer): put one leverage on the table (Diamond or oath-promise). The host matches with an obligation.
Smoke (Complication): the GM reveals a pressure tied to Old Grudges or Two Laws. Resolve it or accept a Rider Clause.
Knot the Braid: on success, create a Feast-Bond [3] timer. On breach, the breaker takes 1–2 SB and it flips to Blood-Owed [3].
Stone Witness: if the Feast-Bond is sworn at the Foedus Stone, reduce the Witness Fading Timer by 1.

start_of_scene_omens.effect: first legal action gains +1d; first boast draws Law Tangle.
Raid Rumor advances once; shortcuts open.
both courts are in session; pick a side or start Law Tangle.
a message arrives; +1d on the next Queen's Audience.
Stipend Arrears counts double value today; smugglers' ears open.
an Utaran relic surfaces; Utaran Patent use is free this scene.

additional_features.crack_light: If the Witness Fading Timer is ≥ 4, the stone also glows. The next legal argument made at the stone is automatically binding — for both sides.
reputation_echoes: Court-Favored — once per session, downgrade Law Tangle to a minor delay; the next document presented is scrutinized (+1 DV).
Raid-Tested — +1 Position when evading Ykrul or Black Banners; supply lines run 1 segment longer.
Neutral Broker — +1d with both oak and marble in a treaty scene; any betrayal earns Blood-Owed [2] from both sides.
Stone-Marked — gained by renewing the treaty. Once per session, reroll a failed social roll involving a Vilikari or a treaty. The stone will ask for a memory in return.

local_patrons.name: The Two-Faced King
local_patrons.description: Justice that wears a laurel and a wolf's tail. He is the stone's first witness.

local_patrons.name: The Hearth Judge
local_patrons.description: The flame that watches both sides of the bargain. She remembers what the stone forgets.

local_patrons.name: The Oak Father
local_patrons.description: The root that holds the law; the branch that signs the treaty. He is older than the stone.

local_patrons.name: The Coin Saint
local_patrons.description: Interest on a handshake; the stone that never sleeps. He profits from the cracks.

local_patrons.name: The Stone's Ghost
local_patrons.description: The Foedus Avatar — what the stone becomes when it forgets too much. It speaks in forgotten clauses and crack-whispers. It is the Hollow's voice in the stone.

boss_archetypes.name: The March Notary
boss_archetypes.description: Quills like daggers — a legalist who buries enemies in citations.
cracks: produce a Foedus Seal to quiet him
a Queen's Audience overrules his filing
if the Witness Fading Timer is at 6+, he gains +1 die in all phases (the stone supports him)

boss_archetypes.name: Ykrul Storm-Rider
boss_archetypes.description: Wolf-cloak, bone whistle — a raid leader who smells weakness in a cracked stone.
cracks: a Wergild Table settles the feud without combat
a Hostage Treaty buys a season's peace
he fights harder if the stone is cracked

boss_archetypes.name: The Prefect's Auditor
boss_archetypes.description: Ecktorial ink on his fingers — a tax officer who closes forts with a tally sheet.
cracks: a Mallus Right transfers jurisdiction to the oak
he carries a piece of the stone in his pocket — if taken, the Witness Fading Timer resets by 2

boss_archetypes.name: The Stone's Ghost
boss_archetypes.description: The Foedus Avatar — what the stone becomes when it forgets too much.
cracks: speak the original treaty aloud (requires a Lethai-al witness)
repair the stone with a memory of a kept promise
sacrifice a personal oath to feed the stone instead of the Hollow

superstitions.name: Bread to the Stone
superstitions.effect: Crumble a crust at the base of the Foedus Stone. Ignore the first Law Tangle penalty.

superstitions.name: Knot the Braid
superstitions.effect: Tie a single knot in a horse's tail. Cancel Annona Late or take −1 die on your next supply roll (your choice).

superstitions.name: Name to the Oak
superstitions.effect: Whisper a dead enemy's name into the hollow of the mallus oak. Gain +1 Effect when collecting wergild from their kin this scene, but mark Obligation to the Elder of Elders.

superstitions.name: Press the Crack
superstitions.effect: Touch the newest crack in the Foedus Stone and speak a promise you intend to break. Gain +1 die on your next deception roll, but the stone will remember your name. The Hollow will too.

decline_and_patronage: In Vilikari society, power flows through the careful balance of multiple legal traditions, the management of frontier diplomacy, and the maintenance of complex oaths and treaties. The Federate King maintains authority through a combination of imperial forms and traditional customs, while local leaders wield influence through their knowledge of both Utaran law and tribal custom. The true power lies with those who can navigate this complex landscape while maintaining the loyalty of their people and the respect of their neighbors. But the stone is cracking. The witnesses are dying. The Vilikari are becoming invisible. The Hollow is learning their laws faster than they remember them. **For the GM:** Patronage in Vilikari society revolves around legal documents, diplomatic relationships, and the ability to command respect from institutions that operate under multiple legal systems. Tie rewards to visible symbols (seals, writs, treaties) that can be challenged, stolen, or voided — and that may crumble if the stone forgets. Let rival legal systems issue conflicting authorities, forcing players to choose whose favor matters more. Use the courts, markets, and frontier posts as arenas for social contests. Remember that Vilikari characters are at home in Ecktoria's counting-houses and Acasia's hedgerow courts alike — but they are never fully trusted in either. That suspicion is their best tool. When the stone cracks fully, that suspicion becomes exile. In Vilikari society, your word is your bond, and your bond determines whether you rule or are ruled. But a bond is only as strong as the stone that witnesses it. And the stone is forgetting.

minor_complications: **Exposure:** March officials or tribal elders take notice.
**Noise:** Levy guards or market patrols are alerted.
**Trace:** Trackers or treaty keepers mark your route.
**Delay:** Lose a favorable legal window or crucial time.
**Supply Strain:** Mark +1 segment on a relevant resource timer.
**Crack Whispers (Vilikari only):** A character hears the stone whispering a forgotten promise. Test Resolve (DV 3) or mark 1 Fatigue.
moderate_setbacks: **Alarm Raised:** The Horse-Reeve or March Notary responds.
**Position Lost:** Legal challenge or border closure costs you advantage.
**Foe Appears:** A rival faction or warband arrives.
**Gear Trouble:** A key item becomes Compromised or Neglected.
**Lock/Barrier:** A simple obstacle now requires a test to overcome.
**Witness Fading:** Advance the Witness Fading Timer by 1 segment.
serious_trouble: **Reinforcements:** Shield-brothers, levy forces, or foreign troops arrive.
**Key Gear Breaks:** A crucial tool or weapon becomes temporarily unusable.
**Major Twist:** Treaty voided, levy called, or border dispute erupts.
**Rail Tick:** Advance a relevant campaign/front timer by 1 segment.
**Condition Applied:** Mark Fatigue 1, Harm 1, or an appropriate Condition.
**Stone Speaks:** The Foedus Stone whispers a forgotten clause that invalidates a character's legal protection for the scene.
major_turns: **Trap Springs:** A prepared danger activates with full effect.
**Authority Arrival:** The Federate King, Queen of Marches, or Elder of Elders intervenes.
**Scene Shift:** A raid hits, the levy is called, or a treaty breaks.
**Patron Omen:** Divine or arcane forces manifest — an omen appears, a blessing is lost, or a curse manifests.
**Narrative Pivot:** The story reframes your objectives unexpectedly.
**Crack Splits:** The Foedus Stone's newest crack widens. One of the party's active Diamonds crumbles to dust.
region_specific: **Seal Crack (1 SB):** A writ loses half its value until re-witnessed.
**Citation War (2 SB):** Increase DV by 1 unless you produce a precedent (spend a Diamond or recall a past ruling).
**Crown Fracture (3+ SB):** A treaty splits; halve a consequence by accepting a rival's seal on your paper (start or tick Two-Law timer).
**Stone Whisper (2 SB, Vilikari only):** The Foedus Stone reveals a forgotten clause. The GM must answer one yes/no question about a treaty or oath in the region.

lore_echoes.title: The Smugglers' Covenant (The Sealed Gate)
lore_echoes.description: Vilikari pilots who run the Kahfagian coast swear by a secret oath to the Unlatched Lock — a threshold that never fully closes. They leave a copper nail at every hidden cove. A captain who breaks the covenant finds that their boat will not cross the tide line; the sea simply refuses to carry them. The Kahfagian Admiralty has tried to bribe the covenant's keeper; he accepted the coin and sank the next morning in calm water. The stone's newest crack appeared that same night.

lore_echoes.title: Saint Theodora of the Dual Writ (The Witness)
lore_echoes.description: A march notary who uncovered a Fenwood spy in the Federate King's court. She forced the spy to sign a confession under both oak and marble, then burned the oak copy and kept the marble one. The spy vanished, but his signature appears on every broken treaty in Vilikari history. Her quill is kept in the Dux's Palace; it writes in lemon juice, and the truth it records cannot be erased by fire or water. The stone's cracks drink the juice.

lore_echoes.title: The Host of the Two Ledgers (The Longhouse Healers)
lore_echoes.description: A hospice near the Foedus Stone is run by gray-robed healers who ask no payment. They treat wounded raiders from both sides of the steppe, and the Ykrul and Ecktorian captains have agreed to a truce around its doors. The Federate King tolerates them because they also hold the rite of the Unbuckled Oath — a ceremony where a knight may renounce a blood-debt without losing honor, by placing their sword on the stone and speaking a single true regret. The stone remembers these regrets. It has many.

lore_echoes.title: The Ostrikari Cousins (The Savage Heart)
lore_echoes.description: The eastern Vilikari, called Ostrikari by lowlanders, are no more savage than any frontier people. Their reputation comes from the bear cults of the upper Wolf Road, where initiates wear cured skins and speak in growls. The Ostrikari do not raid Vilikari villages; they trade furs for iron and send their young to serve as mercenaries in the Black Banners. A Vilikari proverb says: 'The Ostrikari sharpen their teeth on stone, not on kin.' The stone does not mind. It has no teeth left.

lore_echoes.title: The Ninth
lore_echoes.description: In Vilikari courts, the ninth witness called to a mallus (oak-ring) is always a ghost. The wise stop at eight and settle out of court. Those who call a ninth witness find that the ghost speaks the truth — but the truth is always the worst possible version, and the living witnesses remember it as their own. The stone's cracks are full of these truths. The Hollow drinks them.

cross_region_hooks: **Kahfagia (Lantern-Law):** A Foedus Seal may stand in for a Safe-Conduct along a beaconed lane once. Doing so starts Port Clash [2] in the next harbor touched.
**Ecktoria (Imperial Remnants):** An Utaran Patent counts as either Archive Hour (scholars open doors) or Icon License (display symbols) in Ecktorial sites — choose once per session.
**Aelerian Mountains (Pass & Toll):** A Pass-Ring grants priority at dwarf switchbacks; cashing it to bypass inspection spawns Stone Notice [3].
**Direwood (Breath & Bells):** Spending Stipend Arrears for levee labor converts one Direwood Clubs draw into a Ward-Salt Diamond for a scene, then begins Names Disputed [3] with bell-wardens.
**Acasia (Curse & Tithe):** A Wergild Table accepted by a Curse-touched village also clears one Feud Spark timer, but the Hollow gains +1 Attention.
**Lethai-al Silk Bridges:** A Hostage Treaty can be witnessed by a Lethai-al silk-warden, making it binding across the Crimson Valley. The price is a strand of the treaty-bearer's hair.

regional_campaign_starters.title: The Stone That Remembers
regional_campaign_starters.description: The Foedus Stone's newest crack has grown. The Elder of Elders is dying. He knows the original treaty by heart — but he is forgetting. The party must find a witness older than the stone itself before the Elder's last breath. The witness is a Lethai-al elder who lives in the Valewood, and she has not spoken in a century.

regional_campaign_starters.title: The Hostage's Return
regional_campaign_starters.description: A Ykrul hostage string has been returned — cut. The hostage was the Federate King's nephew. The Ykrul claim he escaped. The Vilikari claim he was murdered. The party must find the truth before the passes close for winter. The stone's newest crack has the shape of a footprint.

regional_campaign_starters.title: The Archivolt Fire
regional_campaign_starters.description: Someone has set fire to the Archivolt's oldest wing. The seal-keeper is dead. The only surviving document is a charter granting rights to a canal that no longer exists — but the canal's ghost is now flooding the lower cantons. The party must find the canal's ghost and settle its claim before the flood drowns the capital.
